scope: Follow-up ownership review of tracked FlexLB sources, building on state-api-2026-09-13.json. Foreign untracked replacement classes preserved and excluded from isolated builds.
method: Inspect canonical owner, updates, readers, synchronization, transfer/cleanup and index/cache cost. An inventory or a retained classification is not a proof of every possible concurrency interleaving.

changes.ownership: capacityBlockedHead owns the exact availability; one queue-lock setter changes the head, listener and projection invalidation. Unlock remains guaranteed if removal throws.
Plan.result owns the selected admission; transfer clears the result and close consumes ownership once. waitKey survives close for parking.
One immutable addressProtocols map owns the configured addresses and protocols. Fetch and subscription iterate its keys; a repeated address subscribes once.
Use ConcurrentHashMap.mappingCount, removing a separately incremented/decremented/reset counter. Clear uses the same mutation lock as add/remove and totalMappings updates.

retained_state_review.reason: Queue membership changes and non-queue prediction/status/capacity changes have different invalidation conditions.
References to the same index, not independent copies. PrefillState owns mutations; WorkerBatcher reads under the shared lock.
Thread lifecycle, admission gate and single-owner cleanup transaction are distinct. A stopped thread does not imply completed resource cleanup. Owner detects reentrant self-wait.
Running planners, completed but uncommitted plans, and resource-blocked entries serve different transitions. Removing an index would require scanning a different domain or changing scheduling.
Publication can block on a different resource than routing did; the key must survive admission cleanup until wait registration.
Public progress, storage cleanup, engine ownership and the winning frontend result can advance independently while callbacks are unlocked.
Timer handles provide cancellation; deadline values participate in scheduling; expired records a consumed event. These cannot be inferred from one another during callbacks.
Retirement closes admission before handoffs drain, a continuation can be armed before cleanup starts, and execution-thread identity detects reentrant shutdown.

Hard versus expected demand, queued reservations, acquired dispatch permits and preemption-held resources cover different ownership stages. Aggregates avoid per-admission request-table scans; mutations use admissionLock.

Canonical request ownership, lock-free count, batch capacity and immutable versioned projections serve distinct consumers. Active, suspended, committed and engine-confirmed entries have different membership.
Discovered status generations can exist before the first valid response publishes a routable endpoint. Discovery count is not admission capacity.
Per-domain ownership is needed when one domain removes a shared host. Aggregate is the last published membership for edge-triggered notifications.
Counts all block-engine edges, not map keys. Retained to avoid summing every set for each metrics report; clear now shares its writers lock.
Forward ownership supports per-engine diff and retirement; inverted lookup supports prefix routing. Removing either changes query/update complexity; no claim of a cross-index atomicity redesign.

Ring records occurrence expiry; hash counts support hit queries and repeated keys. Cursor, length, unique count and occurrence count are not interchangeable. Stable final array capacities/masks are not independently mutable facts.
Wall-clock timestamps are observable lifecycle facts; monotonic timestamps measure durations. Different request stages have separate measurement boundaries.
Distinct measurement boundaries plus bounded histogram buckets; sum and max preserve values beyond histogram range. Window replacement defines reset ownership.
Channel membership, executor resources and the no-new-channel gate have distinct lifecycle responsibilities.
Running task membership does not include retained terminal/rejected outcomes or pending stream output. They cannot be collapsed by removing one map without redesigning lifecycle and diagnostics.
